name: Wyoming

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act variant (W.S. 33-44), no registration

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers endorsement contracts (W.S. 33-44-102). It does not use the words name, image or likeness.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) both you and your athlete agent are required to tell your athletic director, if you have an athletic director, at least seventy-two (72) hours prior to entering into an agency contract and again within seventy-two (72) hours after entering into an agency contract; and (3) you may cancel this contract within fourteen (14) days after signing it. Cancellation of the contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
summary: No state license. Give each athlete a disclosure form the day you first contact them. Tell the athletic director 72 hours before and after signing.

steps.detail: Wyoming has no registration. You give a disclosure form to each athlete instead.

steps.text: Fill out the athlete agent disclosure form once
steps.detail: Signed under penalty of perjury. Jobs, training, references, clients, owners and any legal history. You can use another state's recent application instead.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing at least 72 hours before signing
steps.detail: Give them a copy of your disclosure form too. The athlete must also tell the athletic director.

steps.text: Use a signed, written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Attach a copy of your disclosure form to the contract
Put the warning to student athlete box next to their signature
steps.detail: It must be in bold capital letters. Use the state's wording.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director again within 72 hours after signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, if that comes first. Include a copy of your disclosure form.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days of signing
steps.detail: They don't owe you anything if they cancel. They can't give up this right.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) ban pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: Give each athlete the disclosure form on day one
steps.detail: If the athlete contacted you first, within 7 days. You can't sign a contract until you give it, or the contract is void.
Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs. A court can order you to hand them over.

steps.text: Never give the athlete anything of value before they sign
steps.detail: Don't give anything to anyone else to get them to sign, except another registered agent. Never lie, make false promises or ask the athlete to give up their rights.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The statute was read on Justia (2025 edition), and the records section on FindLaw (current as of Jan 1, 2024), not on wyoleg.gov. Confirm on wyoleg.gov.
A 2026 Wyoming law bars NIL pay for high school athletes in WHSAA sports. Its bill number and any effect on agents were not checked.
